intro: The determinant is a single number computed from a square matrix. It tells how much the matrix stretches areas or volumes, and whether the matrix can be undone.

VII.6.01.what: The determinant of a 2-by-2 matrix is a quick cross-multiplication that measures how the matrix scales area.

levels.a: Learns the formula: top-left times bottom-right minus the other diagonal.
levels.c: Knows a zero determinant means the matrix has no inverse.
levels.d: Reads it as the signed area of the parallelogram from the columns.

VII.6.02.what: Cofactor expansion computes a larger determinant by breaking it into smaller ones.

levels.a: Finds minors, the smaller determinants left after crossing out a row and column.
levels.b: Uses the checkerboard pattern of plus and minus signs.
levels.c: Expands a determinant along a chosen row.
levels.d: Picks the row or column with the most zeros to save work.

VII.6.03.what: Computing a determinant efficiently by row-reducing the matrix while tracking how each step changes it.

levels.a: Learns how each row operation changes the determinant.
levels.b: Reduces the matrix to triangular form.
levels.c: Multiplies the diagonal entries of a triangular matrix.
levels.d: Keeps track of all changes to get the original determinant.

VII.6.04.what: Useful rules that make determinants quicker to find without full calculation.

levels.a: Finds a triangular matrix's determinant from its diagonal.
levels.b: Uses the fact that transposing does not change the determinant.
levels.c: Knows two equal rows or a zero row gives determinant zero.
levels.d: Works out what happens when the whole matrix is multiplied by a number.

VII.6.05.what: A matrix has an inverse exactly when its determinant is not zero, a single-number test.

levels.a: Uses a nonzero determinant to confirm an inverse exists.
levels.b: Finds the values that make a matrix lose its inverse.
levels.c: Adds this test to the invertible matrix theorem's list.
levels.d: Finds the determinant of an inverse from the original's.

VII.6.06.what: The determinant measures how a matrix scales area in 2D or volume in 3D, and whether it flips things over.

levels.a: Finds a parallelogram's area from its side vectors.
levels.b: Finds the volume of a slanted box from its edge vectors.
levels.c: Uses the determinant as the area or volume scaling factor of a map.
levels.d: Reads a negative sign as a mirror-image flip.

VII.6.07.what: The determinant of a product equals the product of the determinants, which makes many calculations quick.

levels.b: Uses it to find determinants of products.
levels.c: Finds determinants of powers of a matrix.
levels.d: Explains with an example why sums do not work the same way.

VII.6.08.what: Cramer's rule solves a system of equations using only determinants.

levels.a: Learns the formula: each unknown is a ratio of two determinants.
levels.b: Solves a system of two equations with it.
levels.c: Solves a system of three equations with it.
levels.d: Explains why it is too slow for large systems.

VII.6.09.what: A formula that gives a matrix's inverse directly from determinants of its pieces.

levels.b: Transposes it to get the adjugate.
levels.c: Divides the adjugate by the determinant to get the inverse.
levels.d: Checks the result by multiplying back to the identity.
